scope: Native untimed best-of-three practice using the sourced Arito Irelia registration, with sideboard edits, private field commitment, revealed fields/champions, play-order choice, ordered mulligans, real game results, concessions and match coaching.

rust.scope: All 106 all-targets harnesses passed; after two native-only input corrections, the complete 127-test native harness was rebuilt and rerun. The other 105 executables, their library sources and tests remain byte-identical to the full run.

python.scope: Full existing source/catalog checks. Test/tool/card data inputs are unchanged by the two subsequent native input corrections.

native_controller.scope: Six independently seeded Arito mirror matches reach actual game winners. Sideboard swaps are applied before game two. The alternative-champion unit test explicitly authors a variant registration; it does not alter or mislabel Arito’s preset.

native_interface.scope: Each difficulty uses the same fixed seed and completes one three-game match, repeated at two window sizes with and without captures. These are twelve executed matches, not twelve distinct seeded scenarios. Separate concession fixtures occur only after the played match has finished.

single_game_regressions.scope: Existing Irelia interactions and sourced-preset selection/editor controls at both window sizes, with and without capture.

visual_review.finding: At 1152 by 720 the complete visible card rows, copy counts, chosen champion, paging, undo and confirmation fit; Advanced Mote advice stays in the sidebar.
All three registered battlefield faces and effect text are visible, with separate full-rules and select controls; confirmation is disabled before selection.
The completed three-game history and game point scores are separate from the two-win match markers; the new-match control is visible.
The active game retains physical rune reserves, side point tracks, hand card art and readable location rules, with the game number/match score and explicit concession control.
Sideboard card inspection shows the full Irelia face and complete official rules, with a visible close control.
The normal deck editor remains usable after navigating away from the match lobby; the scrolled list and return/save controls are visible.

source_bridge.revalidation: The complete native test harness, strict all-targets Clippy, release binaries, all twelve series UI runs and eight existing UI runs were rerun after the final native corrections. The unchanged engine/API and integration test artifacts retain their verified hashes.

native_contracts: Use the shared MatchSeries validator and lifecycle without changing the registered main/side pool, legend, runes or battlefield set.
Opponent setup reads only its own observation and commits its battlefield before the human confirmation; both fields then reveal together.
Create hands only after play-order choice. The AI mulligan uses only its own hand and takes place in turn order relative to the human.
Keep the main deck at exactly forty with an eligible chosen champion. Invalid edits disable submission; preview validation cannot commit a choice.
Record each actual game once, show match wins separately from point scores, retire used fields and give the next play-order choice to the previous loser.
Starting a fresh match restores its original registration and available fields. Explicit concessions award a game win; leaving an unfinished match is a separate confirmed action.

findings_resolved: One Irelia capture run lost its X display before any UI checks began. A separate fresh-display rerun of that same release binary passed; the failed attempt and log hash remain attached to its replacement record.
Initial compilation required native integration methods to be visible to their parent module; test AI calls were corrected to the existing engine step_ai interface.

A test incorrectly expected another Irelia champion in Arito’s real sideboard. The positive champion-change test now uses an explicitly authored legal registration; the native UI campaign keeps the exact sourced preset.
Strict Clippy found one collapsible conditional; the final source passes with warnings denied.
Review found setup pausing input for unrelated app screens. The final gate applies only to Practice; a native click test enters and scrolls the deck editor from match setup.

Review found a winning-frame click could reach the old standalone result controls. Registered games no longer render that result panel; the native campaign clicks the old restart coordinates after each actual game win and verifies the series remains intact.
limitations: Native match registration currently offers only the complete Arito Irelia preset. Other presets and saved custom lists remain available for single games; explicit custom registrations are available through Rust/API.

The AI keeps its main deck between games, selects its first unused registered field and chooses to start when designated. Its three difficulty levels govern in-game play; this update does not establish expert matchup or sideboarding strength.
Native draw-agreement controls and resumable match saves are not implemented. The existing API supports intentional draws after game setup.
Timed tournament rounds, judge procedures, best-of-five, broader in-game fidelity and full card coverage remain unfinished.
The card pool stays at 466 of 1079 accepted legal identities; 613 remain unavailable. No new full-gallery acceptance is claimed.
Acceptance uses x86-64 Linux software rendering. No new independent Nix validation was run; the last separately validated Nix source remains 6411bd141a3bff35eb6491e2a6202496045030bf.
